title: WPC Excessive Rainfall Outlook Marginal areas verified below their 5% floor against public flood data in 2022-2026, and both relabels (2017, 2022) came with about 1.5 times larger Marginal areas
abstract: Question: the NWS WPC Excessive Rainfall Outlook (ERO) gives the probability of rain above flash flood guidance within 40 km. WPC raised the category probabilities in 2017 and in 2022 and said that the new numbers only described existing performance. Are the current numbers calibrated against public data, did practice stay the same, and which observations give the reported calibration? Approach: pre-registered test of 3,949 Day 1 outlooks (2016-2026) plus Day 2 and Day 3, on 50,504 CONUS points. An event is a NWS flash flood report or Stage IV 24 h rain above the NOAA Atlas 14 5-year depth within 40 km (primary set U). A designed May-September sample of 606 days (2019-2026) adds 6 h rain above flash flood guidance and above the 6 h 5-year depth. Week-block bootstrap intervals; relabel ratios are compared with placebo dates. Results: hit fractions per category stayed almost constant across the three label eras (Slight 0.125, 0.134, 0.144), while the labels changed by factors of 1.5-2. The 2017 relabel corrected labels that were too low. After 2022, Marginal verified at 0.039 [0.037, 0.041], below its 5% floor; Slight was at its lower edge (0.144 [0.135, 0.152] for at least 15%); Moderate and High agreed. Lead time had almost no effect. Reports alone gave 0.020 and 0.087 for Marginal and Slight; the Era 3 ranges are reached only when any of reports, 24 h or 6 h 5-year rain, or 6 h rain above guidance counts (Marginal 0.073, Slight 0.220). No public set reached the 25% Slight value that WPC quoted. Practice changed: mean Marginal area per outlook rose 1.45 and 1.50 times at the two relabels, and Slight area 1.39 times in 2022, all outside placebo ranges, while total event area did not step. Report hits rose 2.4-2.6 times from the lowest to the highest county population-density third at fixed category; 24 h rain hits did not rise. Limitations: WPC also verifies with USGS gauges, which we did not use; Stage IV artefacts; no Atlas 14 for western Oregon and Washington; FFG proxies are a 50% warm-season sample; Marginal area also grew before the 2017 relabel; other changes near the relabel dates can contribute to the area steps.

display.caption: Day 1 ERO hit fraction (share of category area with an event within 40 km) by category and label era, for public event sets. Grey boxes: the probability range WPC stated in that era. Bars: 95% week-block bootstrap.

After/before ratios at the 2017 and 2022 relabels (Day 1). Marginal area stepped up at both relabels and Slight area in 2022; hit fractions and total event area did not step. Pale bars: placebo 2.5-97.5% range.
Era 3 Day 1 hit fraction by event set on 379 designed May-September days. Marginal and Slight reach their stated ranges only with a union of report and short-duration rain proxies.
